'''Ursula J. Gibson''' is an American materials scientist who specialises in novel core [[Optical fiber|optical fibres]]. <!--Gibson was the president of [[The Optical Society]] in 2019.-->

== Early life and education ==
Gibson was born in [[Sheffield, England]], and moved to the US in the 1960s, living in the [[Philadelphia]] area, then [[Ithaca, New York]]. She received in A.B. in physics from [[Dartmouth College]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://thayer.dartmouth.edu/events/semiconductor-core-glass-fibers|title=Jones Seminar: Semiconductor-core glass fibers—from solar cell to telecommunication applications {{!}} Thayer School of Engineering at Dartmouth|website=thayer.dartmouth.edu|access-date=2019-04-27|archive-date=2019-04-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190427222715/https://thayer.dartmouth.edu/events/semiconductor-core-glass-fibers}}</ref> She received her M.Sc. and Ph.D. from [[Cornell University]] under the supervision of Robert Buhrman in 1978 and 1982, respectively.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.riao.org.mx/optilas_2019/plenary_speakers.php|title=Riao 2019|website=www.riao.org.mx|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://buhrman-group.aep.cornell.edu/people/former-members/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613093247/http://buhrman-group.aep.cornell.edu/people/former-members/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 13, 2018|title=Former Members – Buhrman Research Group|website=buhrman-group.aep.cornell.edu|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://buhrman50.aep.cornell.edu/schedule/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170919094551/http://buhrman50.aep.cornell.edu/schedule/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 19, 2017|title=Featured Speaker Bios – Buhrman: The First 50 Years at Cornell|website=buhrman50.aep.cornell.edu|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> Her graduate research was in the area of [[thin film]] composites.<ref name=":1" /> During her doctoral work, she held a Bell Laboratories Graduate Research Program for Women grant, and spent two summers working at [[Bell Labs]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20161019006487/en/Optical-Society-Elects-Ursula-Gibson-2017-Vice|title=The Optical Society Elects Ursula Gibson as 2017 Vice President|date=2016-10-19|website=www.businesswire.com|language=en|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
After her PhD, Gibson joined the faculty of the [[University of Arizona]], working at the Optical Sciences Center,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://folk.ntnu.no/gibson/people.html|title=Research Group - People - Faculty|website=folk.ntnu.no|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> and was promoted to associate professor.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-ursula-gibson/1489071|title=Prof. Ursula Gibson - AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|access-date=2019-04-27|archive-date=2019-04-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190427222727/http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-ursula-gibson/1489071}}</ref> In 1990, Gibson returned to [[Dartmouth College]], joining the faculty of the [[Thayer School of Engineering]]<ref name="auto"/> where she taught materials science and nanotechnology, participating in interdisciplinary efforts with chemists at Dartmouth and biologists in the [[Norris Cotton Cancer Center]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineergirl.org/2946/Ursula-Gibson|title=Ursula Gibson|website=EngineerGirl|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> She was elected to the board of directors of [[Optica (society)|Optica]] in 2002, and served as the 2019 president of that organization.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2016/the_optical_society_elects_ursula_gibson_as_2017_v/|title=The Optical Society Elects Ursula Gibson as 2017 Vice President &#124; News Releases &#124; The Optical Society}}</ref> 
[[File:Ursula Gibson, Department of Physics 01.jpg|thumb|Ursula Gibson, at the NTNU, Faculty of Natural Sciences]]

Gibson joined the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (NTNU) in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntnu.edu/employees/ursula.gibson|title=Ursula Gibson|last=Fossen|first=Christian|website=www.ntnu.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntnu.no/ansatte/ursula.gibson|title=Ursula Gibson|last=Fossen|first=Christian|website=www.ntnu.no|language=nb|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref>  She was elected to the [[International Commission for Optics|International Commission on Optics]] Bureau in 2011.,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://e-ico.org/contact/bureau14|title=ICO Bureau 2011-2014 {{!}} International Commission for Optics|website=e-ico.org|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> and served as the 2019 president of Optica.  She retired from NTNU and [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kth.se/profile/ujgibson|title=KTH {{!}} Ursula Jane Gibson|website=www.kth.se|access-date=2019-04-27|archive-date=2021-10-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024130821/https://www.kth.se/profile/ujgibson}}</ref> in 2021.  In addition to an NTNU emerita appointment, she is currently an adjunct professor at [[Clemson University]] and emerita at [[Dartmouth College]]<ref>.{{Cite web|url=https://engineering.dartmouth.edu/community/faculty/ursula-j-gibson#|title= Ursula Gibson}}</ref>

Gibson's research on optical materials has been wide-ranging, including polymers, protein crystals and semiconductors, with an emphasis on limited dimension structures such as thin films and waveguides  She holds four patents and has authored 7 book contributions. Gibson's present research is focused on semiconductor-core optical fibers.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=OSA president|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/leadership_and_volunteers/board/ursula_gibson/|website=}}</ref>

Gibson works on optical materials and nanostructures, with a focus on [[Photovoltaics|photovoltaic cells]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://folk.ntnu.no/gibson/|title=Optical Materials and Nanostructures Group|website=folk.ntnu.no|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.solardaily.com/reports/Cheaper_silicon_means_cheaper_solar_cells_999.html|title=Cheaper silicon means cheaper solar cells|website=spacedaily.com|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref>
In particular, she is developing optical fibres with cores made from group IV and [[III-V semiconductor]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1364/OME.8.001435|title=Crystalline Ga ''Sb''-core optical fibers with room-temperature photoluminescence|year=2018|last1=Song|first1=S.|last2=Healy|first2=N.|last3=Svendsen|first3=S. K.|last4=Österberg|first4=U. L.|last5=Covian|first5=A. V. Cuervo|last6=Liu|first6=J.|last7=Peacock|first7=A. C.|last8=Ballato|first8=J.|last9=Laurell|first9=F.|last10=Fokine|first10=M.|last11=Gibson|first11=U. J.|journal=Optical Materials Express|volume=8|issue=6|page=1435|bibcode=2018OMExp...8.1435S|hdl=11250/2560835|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dillard.edu/dillard-newsroom/campus-news/fall-2017-physics-seminar-follow-up.php|title=Dillard University {{!}} Dillard University's Department of Physics welcomed Professor Ursula Gibson, Ph.D.|website=www.dillard.edu|access-date=2019-04-27|archive-date=2019-04-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424182850/http://www.dillard.edu/dillard-newsroom/campus-news/fall-2017-physics-seminar-follow-up.php}}</ref> The semiconductor core materials have [[Nonlinear optics|nonlinear optical]] and [[Electro-optics|electro-optic]] properties, and can be produced in bulk quantities.<ref name=":0" /> The fibres have low thermal mass and large aspect ratios, which allows laser heat treatment resulting in [[Recrystallization (metallurgy)|recrystallization]] of the semiconductor and spatial homogenization or segregation of the constituents in alloy materials. The laser treatment was used by Gibson to write structures of [[germanium]]-rich material in crystalline SiGe core fibres. Rapid directional cooling allows the mixture to form a [[single crystal]], which is optimal for optical transmission, and has superior mechanical properties.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Coucheron|first1=David A.|last2=Fokine|first2=Michael|last3=Patil|first3=Nilesh|last4=Breiby|first4=Dag Werner|last5=Buset|first5=Ole Tore|last6=Healy|first6=Noel|last7=Peacock|first7=Anna C.|last8=Hawkins|first8=Thomas|last9=Jones|first9=Max|date=2016-10-24|title=Laser recrystallization and inscription of compositional microstructures in crystalline SiGe-core fibres|journal=Nature Communications|volume=7|issue=1|article-number=13265|doi=10.1038/ncomms13265|doi-access=free|pmid=27775066|issn=2041-1723|pmc=5079062|bibcode=2016NatCo...713265C}}</ref>  Together with physicist Zahra Ghadyani, Gibson founded the company NorFib to commercialize a fiber-based system for generating electricity with [[solar energy]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://shifter.no/solcellegrunder-zahra-ghadyani-til-topps-gjor-teknologien-bade-billigere-og-enda-mer-miljovennlig/ |title=Solcellegründer Zahra Ghadyani til topps: Gjør teknologien både billigere og enda mer miljøvennlig |language=no |last=Jakobsen |first=Johannes |date=2018-03-01 |access-date=2019-04-29 |website=shifter.no}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=529058781 |title=NorFib AS: Private Company Information |website=[[Bloomberg L.P.]] |access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref>

In 2017, she was elected to Academia Net by the [[Swedish Research Council]].<ref name=":3" />  <!--Gibson served as the 2019 president of [[The Optical Society]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2016/the_optical_society_elects_ursula_gibson_as_2017_v/|title=The Optical Society Elects Ursula Gibson as 2017 Vice President|last=|first=|date=|website=OSA|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/leadership_and_volunteers/officers/ |title=Officers |website=[[The Optical Society]] |access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> -->

Gibson has held visiting positions at the [[United States Air Force Academy]], NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center, [[Tampere University of Technology]] (Finland), [[Chalmers University]] (Sweden), and the [[University of Queensland]] (Australia), among others. She has served as a consultant for many enterprises, including Kodak Inc., the [[US Department of Defense]] and the [[American University of Kuwait]].<ref name=":4" />

*1997 [[NASA]]/[[American Society for Engineering Education]] Visiting Research Fellow<ref name=":2" />
*2001 [[National Academy of Engineering]] Frontiers in Engineering<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.nap.edu/read/6041/chapter/8|chapter=Appendix|year=1998|doi=10.17226/6041|isbn=978-0-309-05983-1|language=en|title=Frontiers of Engineering}}</ref>
*2004 [[NASA]] Network of Educator Astronaut Teachers<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ncesse.org/testimonials/|title=Testimonials {{!}} National Center for Earth and Space Science Education (NCESSE)|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref>
*2008 [[Fulbright fellow|Fulbright Fellow]] at [[VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland]]<ref name=":2" />
*2018 Fellow of [[Optica (society)|Optica]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/fellow_members/recent_fellows/2018_fellows/ |title=2018 OSA Fellows |website=[[The Optical Society]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181101193942/https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/fellow_members/recent_fellows/2018_fellows/ |archive-date=1 November 2018}}</ref> (formerly the Optical Society)
*2019 President of [[Optica (society)|Optica]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.universitetsavisa.no/forskning/2017/06/16/Professor-ved-NTNU-blir-president-i-Optical-Society-of-America-18365966.ece|title=Professor ved NTNU blir president i Optical Society of America|last=Rygg|first=Inga|date=2017-06-16|website=universitetsavisa.no|language=nb|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gibson is married to [[Ulf Lennart Österberg|Ulf Österberg]] who retired in 2024 from the [[Thayer School of Engineering]]; they have three children.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://engineering.dartmouth.edu/magazine/cummings-and-goings-new-and-departing-profs|title=Cummings and Goings: New and Departing Profs {{!}} Thayer School of Engineering at Dartmouth|website=engineering.dartmouth.edu|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref>
